items.title: Akosua Brefowaa joins NPP parliamentary race in Anyaa-Sowutuom

items.title: Accused of ‘emptying the coffers’, Macron mulls spending caps for future French governments
items.summary: Right-wing candidates vying to succeed French President Emmanuel Macron have welcomed his suggestion of a “golden rule” to cap government spending and keep deficits in check, even as they mock the profligacy of his decade in power. Critics of the proposal denounce a budgetary straitjacket imposed on future governments and a distraction from the president’s growing impotence at home.

items.title: Death of Nahel: French police officer who shot dead a teenage boy to stand trial for murder
items.summary: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by the Versailles appeals court. Merzouk's death at the hands of the police sparked intense riots in the sprawling suburbs surrounding Paris.

items.summary: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali will become the first foreign astronaut to board China's Tiangong space station when the latest crew blasts off Wednesday. Ali said he would be carrying "the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis" with him.

The Ukrainian attack on a Russian warship off the coast of eastern Libya has raised questions about Russian and Ukrainian military activity in the country. Gazzini discusses Russia's established military presence in eastern Libya and allegations that Ukrainian forces are operating in the west. items.title: Jensen Huang’s return has calmed markets but fears of an AI bubble still run deep
items.summary: Nvidia's decision to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO pushed the AI computing company's stocks up more than 30 percent Monday. But the model of circular financing increasingly underwriting the AI boom still has some analysts worried that the party can't last forever.

items.title: Collapse of COP31: 'This deal was a bad deal and better no deal than a bad deal'
items.summary: François Picard is joined by Ireland's former environment minister Eamon Ryan following the collapse of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey. "Political science trumps climate science still," Ryan reacted. The talks failed after the European Union and up to 100 countries refused to accept a final text that abandoned earlier commitments to transition away from fossil fuels.

items.summary: A Russian attack killed two people in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia overnight, regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said on Tuesday. Some 40 people, four of them children, were also wounded in the strikes, the governor added. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.
